<reason>Both sides fought hard over the resolution's key clause ("even when drivers strongly oppose"), with CON building a sharp strategic frame: PRO's only real success story, Stockholm, worked because of a guaranteed referendum, so PRO secretly needs a consent mechanism the resolution supposedly forbids. This was clever and rhetorically punchy, especially in the closing ("that sentence is CON's case, not theirs"). But under scrutiny it overreaches: it treats any post-hoc electoral accountability as equivalent to CON's actual proposed model of securing consent *before* imposition, which is a different sequence than what Stockholm did (charge first, ratify later). PRO caught this distinction explicitly (A2.2, A4.1), and more importantly exposed a deeper problem in CON's own examples: Edinburgh and Manchester didn't fail because cities imposed pricing without consent — they failed because voters were asked for consent *first* and refused, which is CON's own preferred sequencing producing zero implementation. CON's rebuttal to this (B2.2) restates the claim without resolving the inconsistency. PRO also pressed a substantive gap that CON never closed: how does "build transit first" get funded before toll revenue exists, given driving stays free the whole time? That circularity, plus PRO's effective reframing of equity (time costs versus cash costs) forced CON's equity argument into a corner (B4.1 essentially conceded CON's whole rebuttal now rests on the untested sequencing plan working). CON's closing was elegant and well-focused, but PRO's substantive economic logic and sharper handling of the Edinburgh/Manchester precedent gave it the more resilient case by the end.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A2.2/A4.1 versus B2.2/B2.3 on Stockholm and Edinburgh/Manchester: PRO's point that Stockholm imposed first and ratified later, while Edinburgh/Manchester's consent-first referenda actually killed the policy outright, undercuts CON's central "consent must precede imposition" claim more than CON's rebuttal manages to repair.</best_rebuttal>
